cases.name: Clarksville Pain Institute / Pain Institute of Nashville

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Saturday, November 14, 2026

cases.name: Johnson Controls Inc. / Johnson Controls Fire Protection LP / Johnson Controls Security Solutions LLC

episodes.practice_note: Fifth Circuit affirmed dismissal of Brook Jackson v. Ventavia Research Group / Pfizer / Icon qui tam (Nov 13, 2026, Judge Willett), applying Polansky v. Executive Health Resources (2023); government declined intervention Jan 2022, later moved to intervene to dismiss; lesson: DOJ dismissal latitude is wide, late-intervention fight is uphill, build the retaliation record early

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Sunday, November 15, 2026

cases.name: Michael Bacon (former Wells Fargo chief security officer) v. SEC

episodes.practice_note: Smith v. U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (D. Guam Oct. 29, 2026): Jarkesy applied to the Administrative False Claims Act, $735,372 HUD award vacated on Seventh Amendment jury-trial grounds; single district court decision, not nationwide; FY2025 NDAA raised AFCA per-claim cap from $150K to $1M

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Monday, November 16, 2026

cases.name: SEC fiscal 2026 enforcement results
cases.amount: $158M+ awarded to 65 whistleblowers; $731M returned to harmed investors

cases.name: Interstate Group Holdings (Defense Personal Property Program survey scores)

episodes.practice_note: CFTC final rule (effective Oct 16, 2026) creates a 30% presumption for whistleblower awards of $5M or less (~82% of meritorious awards expected to qualify); caution from Estate of Jennions v. CFTC (D.C. Cir. July 28, 2026) — award denial upheld where a media article, not the tip, prompted the investigation

cases.name: Firewater Investigations / Lancaster Services / Manhattan Legacy Services (PPP double-dip)

episodes.practice_note: Eleventh Circuit, Brent Berry v. Native American Services Corp. (Nov 12, 2026): summary reversal of Appointments Clause dismissal under Zafirov; Take Care and Vesting Clause arguments remanded; five circuits have now rejected Appointments Clause challenges to qui tam

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Wednesday, November 18, 2026

cases.name: InnovAge Holding Corp. (PACE senior care)
cases.relator: Monita Poudyal and Karen Lapcewich ($4.5M share)

episodes.practice_note: Capitated-payment FCA theory: the false claim is the fixed monthly PACE payment collected while care was not delivered; no corporate integrity agreement mentioned in the announcement; two relators/two suits resolved as one coordinated settlement with a single combined share

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Thursday, November 19, 2026

cases.name: Anthony "Andy" Sanborn / Win Win Win LLC d/b/a Concord Casino (EIDL pandemic relief misuse)
cases.relator: No qui tam relator; government investigation (FBI, IRS-CI, U.S. Postal Inspection Service)

episodes.practice_note: SEC Office of the Whistleblower FY2026 annual report: 29 awards reduced for unreasonable delay in reporting; 140 denials; Foot Locker $148,000 Rule 21F-17(a) penalty for separation agreements purporting to waive whistleblower award rights; 30% award presumption under Rule 21F-6(c) when maximum award is $5M or less

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Friday, November 20, 2026

cases.name: Ruby Scott / Delta Home Health Care LLC (Medicare fraud fueled by illegal kickbacks)
cases.relator: No qui tam relator; criminal prosecution (jury conviction May 2026, E.D. Mich.)

episodes.practice_note: Regeneron / Eylea causation: Nov 19, 2026 D. Mass. ruling that DOJ need not prove 'but-for' causation for the false-certification theory; Judge Saylor's but-for ruling for the AKS 'resulting from' theory affirmed by the First Circuit Feb 18, 2026 (joining Sixth and Eighth Circuits; Third Circuit requires only a 'link'); Judge Gorton's opposite conclusion in Teva; plead both theories

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Saturday, November 21, 2026

cases.name: Honeywell Aerospace Inc. ($2,042,518 cyber-FCA settlement; now a securities class action in D. Ariz., lead plaintiff deadline Nov 23, 2026)
cases.relator: Rachel Tenney, former Honeywell IT employee; $375,823 share (qui tam No. 3:22-cv-129, W.D.N.C.)

episodes.practice_note: DOJ Justice Manual revisions Sept 18, 2026: Section 1-19.000 limits guidance-only FCA enforcement (enforcement must rest on legal requirements; guidance still usable for scienter, standards, and contractual incorporation); Section 4-4.111 requires a dismissal assessment in every declined qui tam and widens the first Granston factor from 'curbing meritless qui tams that facially lack merit' to 'curbing meritless qui tams'; DOJ may re-evaluate dismissal as litigation progresses

episodes.title: Against the Fraud Daily - Sunday, November 22, 2026

cases.name: Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026 (H.R. 11092, introduced Nov 20, 2026) — DOJ whistleblower program paying 10-30% of sanctions over $1M in prediction-market fraud cases; CFTC Nov 13 stay of Kalshi TRUMPSAY markets; Gabriel Perez CFTC settlement Aug 28, 2026 ($107,539.02 disgorgement + $65,000 penalty, three-year ban)
cases.amount: 10-30% of sanctions over $1M (proposed awards); $172,539.02 total Perez sanctions
cases.relator: No relator; proposed DOJ program and CFTC enforcement action (Perez settled without admitting findings)

episodes.practice_note: SEC 90-day award-claim deadline under Rule 21F-10(b): Release No. 104614 (Jan 15, 2026, claim filed ~18 months late, medical-issues excuse rejected, 'extraordinary circumstances' narrowly defined) and Release No. 105185 (Apr 9, 2026, one claimant three months late, another timely but info did not lead to the action); 29 FY2026 awards cut for unreasonable delay in reporting
